points.t: A **new or changing pigmented lesion**, an **ugly duckling**, a **firm growing nodule** (pink or dark), a **dark streak on sole or nail**, or a slowly spreading facial patch.
UV-driven (or non-UV on acral skin) melanocyte mutations (**BRAF**, NRAS, NF1, KIT) with inherited risk (CDKN2A, MC1R).
**NG12**: weighted 7-point score **≥ 3**, or dermoscopy suggesting melanoma → **suspected cancer pathway**; don’t excise or biopsy in primary care.
**Nodular and amelanotic melanoma** (EFG; may not fit ABCD); **acral melanoma** in skin of colour; repeated reassurance of a changing lesion.

cause.lead: A melanocyte cancer driven by UV and genes.
points: UK’s **5th commonest cancer** (~17,500–20,000 a year); rising, esp. > 65; common in 15–34-year-olds.
Risks: **intermittent intense UV / sunburn** (childhood), sunbeds, fair skin (MC1R), many / atypical naevi, family history, previous melanoma, immunosuppression.
**BRAF V600** ~40–50% (BRAF / MEK target); NRAS ~20%; NF1; **KIT** in acral / mucosal.
Radial (flat) then **vertical (nodular) growth**; Breslow tracks the vertical phase.

visuals.caption: Superficial spreading melanoma (left) grows sideways first: flat, irregular, fits ABCDE. Nodular melanoma (right) grows down from the start: raised, firm, growing (EFG), may be pink.
visuals.alt: Two cross-sections: flat spreading pigment versus deep nodule

points: **NICE weighted 7-point**: major (2 each) change in **size, shape, colour**; minor (1 each) **≥ 7 mm, inflammation, oozing, sensation change**. **≥ 3 → refer.**
**ABCDE**: Asymmetry, Border, Colour, Diameter > 6 mm, Evolving; misses nodular / amelanotic.
**Ugly duckling**: different from the person’s other moles.
Subtypes: SSM (commonest), **nodular** (15–30%), **lentigo maligna** (sun-damaged face), **acral lentiginous** (commonest in Black and Asian people), amelanotic.

visuals.caption: Ugly duckling sign: the mole that looks different from all the person’s other moles deserves a closer look.
visuals.alt: Back with similar small moles and one larger irregular dark mole ringed

visuals.caption: Check soles and nails: an irregular dark heel macule, and a nail streak with pigment spreading onto the nail fold (Hutchinson’s sign), suggest acral melanoma.
visuals.alt: Sole with dark heel macule beside a toenail with dark band and fold pigment

points: Dermoscopic + clinical images for teledermatology triage.
Never override clinical concern; skin of colour needs human review.

cards.name: Haemangioma / pyogenic granuloma
cards.clue: Red, bleeds; but amelanotic melanoma mimics PG.

cards.name: Subungual haematoma
cards.clue: Trauma, grows out; no fold pigment.

cards.name: Solar lentigo
cards.clue: Uniform flat brown on sun-damaged skin.

manage.lead: Refer fast; specialist does the rest.

points: **Suspected cancer pathway** (NG12 1.7.1 score ≥ 3; 1.7.3 nodular) **within 1 working day**.
Include images if teledermatology triage exists; document the score and safety-net.
**Excision biopsy with a 2 mm margin** by the skin cancer team → WLE per Breslow.
Sun protection, no sunbeds; full-skin self-checks; first-degree relatives ~2× risk.
Many atypical moles + family melanoma: consider **FAMMM / CDKN2A** (pancreatic cancer link) → genetics.

limits.t: Freeze, shave, laser or ‘watch and wait’ a lesion meeting criteria; reassure because an app is negative.
Refer if not resolving; not more destructive treatment.

items.t: 7-point score **≥ 3** or dermoscopy suggesting melanoma: suspected cancer pathway.
**Firm growing nodule > 1 month** (EFG), even if pink or symmetrical.
New growing dark mark on sole, palm or nail; Hutchinson’s sign.

pearls.t: “Any spot that is **raised, firm and growing**, of any colour, needs to be seen within two weeks.”
Repeated reassurance of a changing lesion is a classic delay pattern.
Check soles, palms and nails in every skin-of-colour presentation.

quiz.q: Commonest subtype in Black and Asian people?
Should primary care excise a suspected melanoma?
quiz.a: No: refer; specialist excision biopsy with a 2 mm margin.
